source: World Bank and KNOMAD bilateral remittance estimates (rounded)
caveat: Corridors are the ones usually reported as the biggest. Amounts differ by year and source, and informal transfers aren't counted.
facts: Remittances sent to poorer countries are bigger than foreign aid and, in many cases, bigger than foreign investment.
For some countries, such as Nepal, Tajikistan and Tonga, money from workers abroad equals a quarter or more of the whole economy.

corridors.note: The biggest corridor in the world: workers in the US sending well over $50 billion a year home.
Indian workers in the US, mostly in tech and health care.
Millions of Indian workers in the Gulf, with the UAE the second-biggest source of India's remittances.
Filipino nurses, carers and others in the US.
Chinese workers and families in the US.
Pakistani workers in Saudi Arabia, a key source of Pakistan's foreign currency.
Egyptians working in Saudi Arabia, among the biggest remittances to Egypt.
Remittances equal to about a fifth of Guatemala's economy.
